articles.title: Calendário lunar de novembro: veja datas da Lua cheia e outras fases | G1
articles.standfirst: Novembro terá Lua nova no dia 9 e Lua cheia no dia 24, que será uma superlua, segundo a Nasa. O mês também terá ocultação de Regulus e pico da chuva de meteoros Leônidas.
articles.summary: Novembro terá Lua nova no dia 9 e Lua cheia no dia 24. A cheia será uma superlua. O mês também terá ocultação de Regulus e pico da chuva de meteoros Leônidas.
articles.body:
A Lua Cheia nasce no Cairo (Egito) em 15 de novembro de 2024. — Foto: REUTERS/Mohamed Abd El Ghany

A Lua cheia de novembro ocorre no dia 24 , às 11h53 , no horário de Brasília. Antes disso, a Lua chega ao quarto minguante no dia 1º, à Lua nova no dia 9 e ao quarto crescente no dia 17.

A cheia deste mês será também uma superlua , segundo a Nasa, a agência espacial norte-americana, já que acontecerá pouco mais de um dia antes de o satélite atingir o perigeu , ponto de sua órbita em que fica mais próximo da Terra.

Novembro ainda reserva outros fenômenos para quem gosta de acompanhar o céu. Na madrugada do dia 3, a Lua passa na frente da estrela Regulus , a mais brilhante da constelação de Leão, em parte do Brasil.

Já no dia 7, a Lua minguante e Vênus vão aparecer próximos no céu, pouco antes do amanhecer.

Veja as datas e os horários das principais fases da Lua, no horário de Brasília:

🌗 Quarto minguante (metade da Lua iluminada, com a parte clara diminuindo): 1º de novembro, às 17h28;

🌑 Lua nova (disco praticamente invisível no céu): 9 de novembro, às 4h02;

🌓 Quarto crescente (metade da Lua iluminada, mas com a parte clara aumentando): 17 de novembro, às 8h47;

🌕 Lua cheia (disco lunar totalmente iluminado para quem observa da Terra): 24 de novembro, às 11h53.

❗ Preste atenção no seu fuso, pois os horários mudam de acordo com ele. No Acre, por exemplo, a Lua cheia ocorre às 9h53; em Fernando de Noronha, às 12h53.

Já quem espera um eclipse como o eclipse lunar parcial visto no fim de agosto terá de aguardar: novembro não terá um eclipse do tipo.

O próximo eclipse lunar ocorrerá em fevereiro de 2027 , mas será penumbral e quase imperceptível a olho nu. Um eclipse parcial volta a ser visível em todo o Brasil só em janeiro de 2028 , e um total, em junho de 2029.

A Lua não produz luz própria. O brilho que vemos no céu é a luz do Sol refletida em sua superfície.

Em qualquer momento, metade da Lua está iluminada pelo Sol. O que muda ao longo do seu ciclo então é quanto dessa parte iluminada conseguimos enxergar da Terra, conforme o satélite percorre sua órbita ao redor do planeta.

Na Lua nova, a face iluminada fica voltada principalmente para o lado oposto ao da Terra, e o disco lunar praticamente não aparece no céu. Nos dias seguintes, a parte iluminada visível aumenta.

No quarto crescente , aproximadamente metade do disco que vemos está iluminada. Essa parcela continua aumentando até a Lua cheia , quando praticamente toda a face voltada para a Terra aparece iluminada.

Depois, ocorre o caminho inverso: a área iluminada visível diminui até o quarto minguante e segue encolhendo até uma nova Lua nova.

➡️ O intervalo entre duas luas novas consecutivas é chamado de lunação .

O ciclo que começa em 9 de novembro termina em 8 de dezembro e dura cerca de 29 dias e meio. Por isso, as fases da Lua não acompanham exatamente o começo e o fim dos meses do calendário.

Lua cheia é vista no início do eclipse lunar no Cairo, no Egito, nesta sexta-feira (28). — Foto: Amr Abdallah Dalsh/Reuters

A Lua cheia ocorrerá em 24 de novembro , às 11h53 , no horário de Brasília. Como isso acontece durante o dia, o melhor momento para observá-la será depois do pôr do Sol.

Em São Paulo (SP), a Lua nasce por volta das 18h57. No Rio de Janeiro (RJ), às 18h41; em Recife (PE), às 17h33; em Brasília (DF), às 18h44; e em Porto Alegre (RS), às 19h34.

A Lua cheia também será considerada uma superlua , porque ocorrerá quando o satélite estiver próximo do ponto de sua órbita em que fica mais perto da Terra.

No dia 24, a Lua estará a cerca de 361 mil quilômetros do nosso planeta. No dia seguinte, essa distância será ainda menor, de aproximadamente 359 mil quilômetros .

Essa proximidade faz com que a Lua pareça um pouco maior e mais brilhante do que em outras luas cheias.

Ao nascer, próxima ao horizonte, a Lua também poderá parecer maior devido a uma ilusão de ótica e apresentar tons amarelados ou avermelhados por causa da atmosfera.

Na madrugada de 3 de novembro, a Lua vai passar na frente de Regulus, a estrela mais brilhante da constelação de Leão, e escondê-la temporariamente.

Em São Paulo (SP), a estrela deve desaparecer atrás da Lua por volta das 4h43. Em Brasília (DF), isso ocorre às 4h32; em Belo Horizonte (MG), às 4h44; e em Curitiba (PR), às 4h41.

A Lua estará minguante , com cerca de um terço de sua superfície visível iluminada.

O fenômeno, porém, não poderá ser observado em todo o Brasil. Em cidades como Recife (PE), Fortaleza (CE) e Belém (PA), a estrela não será encoberta.

Imagem feita de Pitangueiras (SP), na região de Ribeirão Preto (SP), por câmera fotográfica de conjunção entre Lua e Vênus. — Foto: José Carlos Salerno

Na madrugada de 7 de novembro, a Lua minguante e Vênus também vão aparecer muito próximos no céu, pouco antes do amanhecer.

Para observar, será preciso olhar para o horizonte leste. A aproximação é apenas aparente, já que os dois astros continuam separados por milhões de quilômetros no espaço.

No dia 15 de novembro, Marte e Júpiter também vão aparecer próximos no céu e poderão ser observados antes do nascer do Sol.

Novembro também será marcado pela chuva de meteoros Leônidas , formada por fragmentos deixados pelo cometa 55P/Tempel-Tuttle .

O fenômeno atinge seu pico em meados do mês, e a melhor oportunidade de observação no Brasil deve ocorrer na madrugada de 18 de novembro.

Em São Paulo (SP), o período mais favorável deve começar por volta das 2h e seguir até pouco antes do amanhecer, quando a constelação de Leão estará mais alta no céu.

Para observar os meteoros, não é necessário usar telescópio ou binóculo. O ideal é procurar um local escuro, longe das luzes das cidades, e observar uma área ampla do céu.

No dia 20 de novembro, Mercúrio poderá ser observado antes do amanhecer, quando atingirá sua maior distância aparente do Sol no céu.

Já no dia 25, Urano estará em uma posição favorável para observação, permanecendo acima do horizonte durante boa parte da noite.

Por ter brilho fraco, porém, será mais fácil encontrá-lo com binóculos ou telescópios .

A luminosidade da Lua, que estará quase cheia, também poderá dificultar a observação do planeta.

articles.title: Normal blood pressure may not tell the whole story: Scientists discover a brain ‘switch’ that could secretly raise cardiovascular risk and open new avenues for heart and brain treatments
articles.summary: An estimated 1.4 billion adults aged 30 to 79 around the world had hypertension, or high blood pressure in 2024, making it nearly 33% of the population as
articles.body: An estimated 1.4 billion adults aged 30 to 79 around the world had hypertension, or high blood pressure in 2024, making it nearly 33% of the population as per a WHO report. While, this data points towards the number of people who have been diagnosed with hypertension, and estimated 600 million adults with hypertension are not even aware. Blood pressure is a more confounding issue than meets the eye. If you've visited your doctor, no matter what problem you went approaching for, you would’ve been asked to get your blood pressure checked.Blood pressure is one of the first things we measure when we visit a doctor, and the numbers often become a quick way of understanding how well our cardiovascular system is functioning. However, what if a normal reading does not always tell us the complete story? Scientists have discovered a small group of nerve cells in the brain that helps keep blood pressure stable as the body moves between different states of activity. The discovery offers a new understanding of how the brain regulates cardiovascular health and why fluctuations in blood pressure could matter even when its average readings appear normal.The research, carried out by Scientists at the University of Virginia School of Medicine, investigates how the brain helps the body maintain steady blood pressure during everyday activities. Published in the Circulation Research journal, the study identifies a group of brainstem neurons that appear to play an important role in preventing sudden changes in blood pressure. The findings of this can eventually help researchers understand certain cardiovascular risks and develop treatments which focus not only on blood pressure levels but also on regulating themWhat happens when blood pressure appears normal?Our Blood pressure is not a fixed measurement that remains unchanged throughout the day. It naturally rises or falls as we sleep, eat, wake up or if unfortunately we find ourselves in situations that can immediately shoot this vital up. These changes are all part of our body’s response to different situations, allowing the cardiovascular system to adjust to the changing needs. However, the recent research suggests that while the average blood pressure reading may not be indicative of a heart problem, rapid or excessive changes in the blood pressure reading throughout the day can point towards a heart disease, stroke and brain injury, even if it lies in the normal range.The University of Virginia researchers have therefore investigated the neural mechanisms responsible for maintaining this balance. Their attention turned towards the brainstem, a region of the brain involved in essential automatic functions, including the regulation of breathing, heart rate and blood pressure. Within this region, the researchers studied a small population of nerve cells that play the role of maintaining steady blood pressures.These cells are located in the rostral ventrolateral medulla, an area involved in controlling the body's cardiovascular responses and researchers wanted to understand how these neurons contribute to blood pressure stability as an individual moves between different behavioural states. The findings suggest that losing even a few hundred of these cells can disrupt the mechanisms that stabilise blood pressure, causing fluctuations even when its average reading remains normal.What could this discovery mean for future treatments?The new research findings raise a possibility that disruptions in similar brain-based mechanisms could contribute to blood pressure instability in other circumstances, including situations where average readings appear normal. Understanding how these neurons work could eventually help scientists develop treatments designed to improve blood pressure stability.The health of our brain and heart is trickier to understand because the two are so deeply intertwined, as the body's responses to its environment can signal a cause for concern for both. By identifying a group of brain cells that helps maintain this delicate balance, scientists have opened another avenue for investigating how cardiovascular and neurological health intersect. However, at its current stage, the discovery remains an important step towards understanding the relationship between the brain and cardiovascular health, two aspects of our well-being that are intrinsically tied to one another.

articles.title: Common daily fiber supplement was found to significantly reduce knee pain and improve muscle strength in a new study, offering a cheap and easy option for the millions of people living with painful, stiff knees
articles.summary: Very recently, the internet was abuzz with conversations about protein and then even fibre, with the humble macronutrients taking centre stage in
articles.body: Very recently, the internet was abuzz with conversations about protein and then even fibre, with the humble macronutrients taking centre stage in discussions aboutr health and nutrition. However, the food pyramid we have all grown up studying, simple as it may appear on paper, is far more complex to follow in practice. The human body relies on an intricate network of nutrients and compounds that come together to keep the body healthy and fucntion, meaning no single fod group can meet all our meeds, but researchers wondered if a single food cannot allay all our concerns can one macronutrient be involved in helping alleviate a major one? .While joint pain is commonly associated with aging and the gradual deterioration of cartilage, researchers are increasingly investigating whether the answer to managing it could also lie somewhere beyond the joints themselves. A new clinical trial led by researchers at the University of Nottingham, published in the journal Nutrients has now discovered that a daily prebiotic fibre supplement could help alleviate knee osteoarthritis pain, improve grip strength and make the body less sensitive to painful stimuli.How a daily fibre supplement could help with knee painThe supplement which researchers focused on was inulin, a naturally occurring dietary fibre that is easily found in foods such as chicory. It is a prebiotic dietary fibre that can be beneficial for gut health, especially helpful in regular, easy digestion. Moreover, unlike nutrients that are broken down and absorbed in the small intestine, inulin passes into the large intestine, where it can be fermented by gut bacteria. It is classified as a prebiotic, meaning that it provides nourishment for certain beneficial microorganisms living in the digestive system.Dr. Afroditi Kouraki, primary author of the study from the School of Medicine at the University of Nottingham notes that adding a simple fibre supplement to breakfast or yoghurt could meaningfully reduce pain and improve physical function. The researchers investigated whether introducing this fibre into the diet could influence knee osteoarthritis, a condition in which changes to the tissues within a joint can lead to pain, stiffness and difficulty performing everyday activities. Although existing approaches such as pain medication and physiotherapy can help manage symptoms, persistent discomfort can make regular physical activity difficult for some people.With findings that seem encouraging the trial itself was a short one, lasting only 6 weeks: the INSPIRE, a randomised clinical trial with 136 participants, out of which 117 adults with knee osteoarthritis completed the assesments. Participants were divided into four groups receiving inulin alone, digitally supported physiotherapy exercises alone, a combination of the two, or a placebo. The researchers then assessed changes in pain, physical function, muscle strength and sensitivity to painful stimuli.The results showed that both inulin supplementation and physiotherapy-supported exercise reduced knee pain compared with the placebo. However, participants receiving inulin also experienced improvements in grip strength and pain sensitivity, benefits that were not observed in the physiotherapy-only group. These findings suggest that dietary interventions may influence aspects of pain and physical function that extend beyond the affected joint.The connection between gut bacteria and pain"Our findings suggest that targeting gut health with a prebiotic supplement is a safe, well-tolerated, and effective way to reduce pain in people with knee osteoarthritis,” says Dr. Kouraki. One of the most interesting aspects of the research is the possible role played by the gut microbiome, the community of microorganisms living in the digestive tract. The role of these microbes is more than just to assist in the process of digestion, as they also produce substances which interact with the body’s biological processes including effects on the pathways involved in inflammation and pain.When gut bacteria ferment inulin, they produce short-chain fatty acids, including butyrate. This compound supports the intestinal environment and is involved in biological processes that may influence inflammation. During the trial, researchers observed increased butyrate levels among participants taking inulin, pointing towards the supplement altering activity within the gut microbiome.The study also found an increase in glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), a hormone released by the gut that plays a role in regulating blood sugar and appetite. Interestingly, higher GLP-1 levels were associated with better grip strength among participants. However, this association cannot determine that the hormone directly caused an improvement. Rather, it provides researchers with perhaps an explanation for how changes in the digestive system could possibly be connected to muscle function.A noteworthy observation of the study is the difference in participant retention across the treatment groups. Only 3.6 per cent of those receiving inulin alone dropped out of the study, compared with 21 per cent of those assigned to physiotherapy-supported exercise alone. This suggests that the supplement may be easier for participants to incorporate into their daily routines, although the difference in dropout rates does not establish that it is more effective than exercise.Could fibre become an additional approach for managing arthritis?The importance of this research’s findings becomes more resounding when we look at the number of people struggling with osteoarthritis pain. The findings are particularly relevant because managing osteoarthritis often requires approaches and courses of treatment that can be sustained overtime. The study conducted by the researchers offers a wonderful insight into how the alleviation of arthritis pain does not merely begin and end with the joints, but also involves a major factor: our gut health and dietary habits. While the research only nudges at possible treatment plans, health begins at home, or more precisely, in your kitchen, especially at a time when what you eat and the quantity you consume may be holding more answers than ever thought before.

articles.title: Cleopatra’s eye makeup secret? Ancient Egyptians used lead-based kohl that may have boosted the body’s immune defences and helped fight eye infections
articles.summary: Make-up as an art never began simply to enhance the appearance but to draw courage from what was not mere beauty, but power and protection.
articles.body: Make-up as an art never began simply to enhance the appearance but to draw courage from what was not mere beauty, but power and protection. Mistaken for mere garb, its long expanse across myriad empires and dynasties has symbolized unyielding power, stretched in strokes of black kohl and rosy rouge, painting a face not just to appease eyes, but to amass attention. However, National Geographic brings attention to something even more fascinating about the beauty rituals of the ancient world, especially when we discover that what people applied extended into what was believed to be medicinal.Ancient Egypt, a civilisation remembered for its elaborate jewellery, striking silhouettes and distinctive eye makeup, offers a fascinating example of how medicine and beliefs about protection could exist alongside one another. The dark, elongated eyes associated with Cleopatra, last ruling queen and pharaoh of the Ptolemaic kingdom of Egypt, has till date caught our attention. With researchers in the last few decades suggesting that certain compounds used in ancient Egyptian eye makeup could have stimulated the body’s immune defenses, a curious conversation between archaeology and modern science has now opened up.The ancient Egyptian practice of wearing kohlEye makeup was not an exclusive privilege of Egypt's queens or ruling elite. Men and women across different levels of Egyptian society wore cosmetics around their eyes, with black and green powders being among the familiar choices. Known as kohl, the dark pigment was used to define the eyes, accentuate their shape and create the distinctive appearance that continues to inspire contemporary beauty trends. Its significance, however, extended beyond aesthetics. Ancient Egyptian beliefs associated the eyes with divine protection, while cosmetics were also thought to protect the wearer against illness and the harsh conditions of the environment.The eye held considerable religious significance in Egyptian culture, with symbols such as the Eye of Horus associated with protection and well-being. Applying makeup could therefore form part of a wider understanding of personal appearance, spiritual protection and health. Historical medical texts also record the use of preparations for eye ailments, suggesting that cosmetics and remedies did not always occupy entirely separate categories in the ancient world.What scientists discovered in ancient makeupThe possible medicinal properties of Egyptian kohl attracted renewed attention when French researchers investigated its chemical composition. Their research, published in the journal Analytical Chemistry in January 2010, examined the relationship between certain lead compounds found in ancient Egyptian cosmetics and the body's response to them.Chemical analyses of ancient cosmetic samples had identified several lead-containing ingredients. Two compounds, laurionite and phosgenite, were particularly interesting because they do not occur naturally in the form used in cosmetics and appear to have been deliberately prepared. This raised questions about whether ancient Egyptian cosmetic makers understood something about the properties of the substances they were producing.The research team, including Christian Amatore and colleagues, investigated how these compounds interacted with cells. Their experiments found that very low concentrations of lead ions could stimulate skin cells, known as keratinocytes, to produce nitric oxide. This molecule plays several roles in the body, including helping regulate immune responses and contributing to defences against certain disease-causing microorganisms.The finding possibly offers an insightful explanation for why some ancient cosmetic preparations might have had a medicinal function in addition to a decorative purpose. Rather than establishing that the makeup itself prevented infections in people, however, the study demonstrated a biological response under laboratory conditions. The distinction matters because a reaction observed in cultured cells does not automatically translate into a proven health benefit when a substance is applied to the human body.Could kohl have helped protect the eyes?Eye infections would have posed a serious problem in the ancient world, and the Egyptians' use of eye preparations for health-related purposes makes the researchers' findings particularly interesting. If certain ingredients encouraged the production of nitric oxide, they might have supported some of the body's natural defences against bacteria.The researchers estimated that the quantities of the relevant compounds in the makeup could have produced a substantial increase in nitric oxide production. This led them to propose that the substances may have been intentionally prepared for their beneficial properties. However, the question of whether ancient Egyptians consciously understood the underlying chemistry remains unresolved. It is possible that generations of experience informed their practicesThe story of Egyptian eye makeup is, therefore, far more fascinating than beauty hiding a scientific secret. It takes us back thousands of years, reminding us that even something as familiar as the kohl we apply around our eyes can carry echoes of a civilisation’s beliefs, knowledge and ways of looking at the world. While we may never know whether Cleopatra’s kohl actually helped protect her eyes from infections, we certainly know that her striking eyes and the illustrious queen herself continue to leave us in awe of the beauty she once beheld.
